event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
Revisited the original concern: a reused attachment or leaked paused state could leave a reopened session showing old output and ignoring new work. The surviving test checks distinguish that failure from a healthy fresh attachment.

## Details
Synthesis checked the complete caller, terminal.spec.ts:445-563. Before leaving it stamps the live grid and retains the owned WebSocket and hook. After switching, it requires a defined replacement grid with a different marker, the old socket CLOSED, and all four old socket handlers null. After returning, it waits for the requested session's reveal, checks a fresh grid and defined distinct hook, requires the old output marker, and sends marker-after-reopen, requiring the live echo. The final echo is backend-independent evidence against a persistently paused or dead new attachment; the removed zero counters were an implementation-specific observation, not the only liveness observable. SPEC_impl.md, Terminal widget: the grid island: 'the page applies every message as it arrives and sends no flow control of its own.' The applicable guarantee remains SPEC.md, Terminal experience: 'Reconnecting replays the terminal so the session looks as it would have had the client stayed attached'. Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed by source, no execution. proposed_drop: preserve the original proposed drop, now supported by the surviving socket teardown, object identity, replayed old marker and post-reopen live echo checks rather than absence of the old counters alone. possible_cover: none; no queue or coverage sources searched. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route in this assertion change. Caveat: the live echo establishes liveness for this fixture, not a broad stress proof of server flow control. Prior wording called watermark an input path; the removed counters measured output backpressure, and this revision corrects that terminology.

event.summary: held-replay helper claims history is applied before its oracle proves it
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
The revised test helper describes a fully applied replay, but it only waits for the replay marker. Older terminal output can still be queued at that point. This is a test synchronization/documentation defect; no shipped output loss has been demonstrated.

## Details
The changed docstring says 'the replay has arrived and been applied to the still-hidden terminal'. The helper at :136-154 polls only __farhelmIslands[el].test.replay.heldReason == marker. terminal.js:4073-4082 handles replay_complete by immediately calling endCatchUp, whose :3886-3888 held-marker path sets heldReason without waiting for the grid's history queue. grid-terminal.js:1876-1930 drains queued history in bounded slices scheduled on later animation frames/message-channel tasks. term.ts:162-215 explicitly states and implements that unapplied history is absent from text reads, and terminal-readiness.ts:40-55 waits only for revealed. Therefore neither this helper nor the subsequent reveal wait establishes the newly documented applied-history boundary. SPEC_impl.md, The grid client, explicitly says the client applies a large history 'in slices between frames so that the screen stays usable'. terminal.js:3774-3776 also explicitly says history may still be applying when the screen reveals.

The backend-independent completeness concern remains narrower than a product bug: the agent test at :371-375 reads only spam-line-200, which is in the current screen after spam 200; the tab test waits only for TABSPAM-200. Those observables do not independently prove historical rows arrived. That weak last-line assertion was already present before this commit, so it is not claimed as newly introduced missing-history behavior. The newly changed helper contract should say the replay marker arrived and the current screen was applied, with history potentially pending. If callers need fully applied history, add a separately named history-drained oracle and assert an older line as well; do not make all held-state tests wait for a stronger boundary indiscriminately.

Suggested bucket: other, confined to test synchronization documentation and its overstated observable. Confidence: confirmed by source/contract analysis; no execution. proposed_drop: false for the newly false helper contract. Preserve prior proposed drop for bufferBytes/bufferChunks/bufferedBytes themselves: those removed controls describe the retired byte-stream buffer and are not current grid guarantees. The previous broad c2 dismissal is narrowed by this revision, not silently removed. possible_cover: none; no queue or coverage sources searched. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route; missing test evidence alone does not prove such harm. Caveat: the current callers' hidden/visible, marker-reason, first-frame-tail and live-input assertions remain useful and this finding does not require reveal to block on all history.

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
Revisited whether the simplified checks could pass while old tab attachments survive, hidden tabs have unusable geometry, or a fresh tab displays residue. The surviving assertions still discriminate those failures.

## Details
The full teardown caller (:668-723) establishes exactly three original registry keys, retains all three socket/component objects, requires all original sockets CLOSED after leaving and both tab islands absent, then waits for the exact original nonempty registry key set before comparing every new grid against the retained components. Thus deleting the old-renderer fallback does not turn the instance comparison into an empty-array success. Production terminal.js:4313 builds the grid, :4660 publishes the primary grid, and :4668 publishes the same object into each island record, matching these reads. The hidden-geometry caller (:1294-1324) confirms the tab is hidden, checks its element's real width/height and nondegenerate grid.size(), then selects it and requires a live shell marker. Resize callers (:1590-1661) inspect committed grid.model rows/columns and require changes on confirmation open/window resize and restoration on confirmation cancel, preserving the program-visible sizing observable. The clean-screen test uses grid.snapshot().lines with cursor.y; grid-terminal.js:2091-2105 returns screen rows and cursor together, with history separate, so its coordinate space remains valid. SPEC_impl.md, The grid client: 'Drawing still rounds cells at the supervisor-committed size'. SPEC_impl.md, Terminal widget: the grid island: 'Every terminal runs in a terminal host' and the browser draws a grid stream.

Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed by source, no execution. proposed_drop: retain the original no-active-renderer/coordinate-regression basis, supplemented by the actual nonempty-instance, closed-socket, real-geometry and live-input assertions. possible_cover: none; no queue or coverage sources searched. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route from these changes. Caveat: object replacement plus closed sockets does not measure heap reclamation; neither the removed fallback nor this patch promised a heap measurement. The same grid branch and clean-screen coordinate use already existed before the patch.

event.summary: comment-only substrate updates keep independent restart and live-input witnesses
event.detail:
Reviewed commits: 61e632323dbc6b4a35ed27bf5b9833102ffd5a4e and 4b489b4f2eeade14f119b186ecb16eeaaf027021

## TLDR
Revisited whether renamed terminal mechanisms hide an unchanged test that no longer proves restart history, live clipboard delivery or Unicode replay. The inspected callers retain witnesses for those behaviors; the assigned patches change their comments only.

## Details
Restart retention (:1022-1086) sends a unique prior-run marker, pushes it into history with spam 60, then sends a distinct grid-only marker. After restart it polls for prior marker before the last new-run banner and absence of the grid-only marker in one text snapshot. This genuinely distinguishes retained history from merely preserving the visible screen. SPEC.md, Lifecycle operations: 'the terminal is replaced by a new one for each run, which starts with the old one's scrollback above a blank screen in default modes' and 'Restart does NOT preserve the previous run's last visible screen'. Clipboard callers (:330-347, :369-407, :431-450) hold emission behind read, use attachSession before Enter, and observe either the exact clipboard value or a printed post-query sentinel. attachSession delegates to waitForSessionReady (term.ts:319-336), whose socket-identity, OPEN, reveal and actual input-focus checks are in terminal-readiness.ts. Thus the header's weaker statement that OPEN is required does not imply the actual callers send before replay. The read-query leg seeds and observes a secret before querying and checks outbound data plus the unchanged real clipboard; this patch removes no security assertion. Unicode replay (:130-177) requires a different socket, marker-ended reveal, exact buffer and DOM rows, cursor coordinates and a fresh continue reply after reconnect. Flood (:217-288) observes xy before erase, waits for live echo:x before Ctrl-C and checks for a forbidden subsequent echo over its observation window. Those are backend-independent witnesses; the 4b patch changes only the historical fixture's verb tense. Grid-client comment changes retain the same assertions and the same documented rounding/input encoding as recorded previously.

Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed by source/contract analysis; no execution. proposed_drop: preserve original comment/contract consistency basis, now supplemented by the actual surviving restart ordering/absence and post-attach command witnesses. possible_cover: none; no queue or coverage sources searched. Could-be-highest: the clipboard read contract is security-sensitive, but the assigned change only rewrites the launch/replay explanation and removes no security behavior or test observable; no substantive highest issue is being dropped by specification acceptance. Caveat: this does not independently certify clipboard security across all wire frames or re-review unchanged test limitations outside the assigned edits. No current input-loss or terminal-history loss was observed or reproduced.

event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
Discovery considered whether simplifying the theme/frame tests makes them inspect an unrelated wrapper or lets a missing renderer pass. The selectors still address the actual painted grid surface and retain the observed background and geometry checks.

## Details
terminal.spec.ts:113-133 reads the defined primary grid's inline background, computed grid background and computed outer terminal background; it requires the exact expected rgb value and equality to the wrapper. At :150-213 the selected outer island scopes its grid surface, and the test checks frame appearance through Settings and host appearance changes while surface colors and client dimensions stay fixed. grid-terminal.js:341-344 creates distinct grid-terminal and grid-terminal-screen elements, :829-834 paints the grid root's defaults.bg inline, and app.css:8614-8615 scopes the host-colored shadow to the outer direct child terminal. SPEC.md, Terminal experience: 'The terminal background, text palette and size do not change.' Thus the new selectors do not substitute an unpainted test property for the old surface observable. The grid branch already used the same inline/background checks before this commit; this patch removes the retired alternative. The test does not assert every ANSI palette entry, and that is not claimed as a new lost assertion. Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed source-only; no runtime execution. proposed_drop: no new surface/selector oracle defect established by the assigned simplification. possible_cover: none; no queue or coverage sources searched. Could-be-highest: no; these visual test assertions have no established security or loss-of-work route. Material caveat: background checks do not independently certify every row's foreground/palette rendering, and a correct current implementation alone would not refute a removed distinct assertion; none was removed from the grid branch here.

## TLDR
Discovery considered whether the failed-mount test now passes when a half-created grid remains, because checking an unpublished singleton alone cannot prove disposal. The current test's guard/retry observable remains intact; the broader disposal limitation predates the entire pinned range.

## Details
At reviewed terminal.spec.ts:795-850 the sabotage makes WebSocket construction throw after grid creation, waits for the failure banner, checks the primary grid singleton is absent, restores WebSocket, bounces selection and requires the same session to reveal and show its ready banner. The removed assertion checked the retired singleton in addition to that same grid singleton, not DOM teardown or grid.dispose. Exclusive-base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a terminal.spec.ts:814-866 has the same WebSocket failure boundary, singleton-only teardown observation and same-session remount check, and its introductory comment already claims disposal. ## TLDR
Discovery considered whether grid-only row selectors stop testing the retained non-live screen or mistake an active replacement for a snapshot. The test retains explicit detached-state, painted-row and real-gesture witnesses.

## Details
The complete caller (:775-864) requires an empty island registry before observing the held screen; reads the marker from visible DOM instead of an unpublished model; measures a visible grid row containing each link before deriving coordinates; verifies drag does not open a web target; verifies the click opens the exact URL or downloads the exact file bytes; makes a real selection and observes the clipboard argument/value; and reasserts that no island attached. terminal.js:1566-1570 keeps the island's actual grid component as the held snapshot before unmount, and grid-terminal.js:2075-2085 freezes sending/resizing while retaining the same screen, selection and links. grid-terminal-row is the same DOM row class created at grid-terminal.js:620, so narrowing the selector still reaches the frozen component's actual painted rows. Exclusive-base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a terminal-reconnect.spec.ts:801-856 has the same grid selector alternative, geometry calculation and concrete gesture assertions; :1893-1899 and :2026-2032 already count the grid screen alongside the old renderer.
